title: One-Variable Data: Distributions and Measures
subtitle: Master mean, median, mode, range, and data spread — from lists, tables, and graphs

sections.title: The Three Measures of Center
sections.content:
When analyzing a single variable's data set, the SAT tests three key measures:

- **Mean** (average): sum of all values ÷ count
- **Median**: the middle value when data is sorted. With an even count, average the two middle values
- **Mode**: the value that appears most frequently

And two measures of spread:
- **Range**: maximum − minimum
- **Standard deviation / spread**: measures how spread out data is from the mean

sections.title: Steps to Find the Median
sections.content:
1. **Sort** the data from smallest to largest
2. If **odd** count: median = the middle number
3. If **even** count: median = average of the two middle numbers

steps.description: With 8 values (even), average the 4th and 5th values

sections.title: Example: Median from a Bar Graph
sections.problem: A battery charged for 15 days with: 6 days at 0 kWh, 1 day at 8 kWh, 2 days at 9 kWh, 2 days at 11 kWh, 2 days at 16 kWh, 2 days at 23 kWh. What is the median?

steps.description: With 15 values, the median is the 8th value

sections.tip: For frequency tables or bar graphs, write out ALL individual values (including repeats) before finding the median position.

sections.title: Type 2: Comparing Mean, Median, and Mode
How Distribution Shape Affects the Measures
sections.content:
The shape of the distribution tells you the relationship between mean, median, and mode:

- **Symmetric (bell-shaped):** mean ≈ median ≈ mode
- **Right-skewed (long tail to the right):** mode < median < mean
- **Left-skewed (long tail to the left):** mean < median < mode

The **mean is pulled toward the tail** because extreme values affect the sum. The **median is resistant** to extreme values.

sections.title: Example: Order the Three Measures
sections.problem: A college class has ages: mostly 18-20, with a few students aged 35-45. A frequency table shows more young students than old. Which gives the correct order of mean, median, and mode?

steps.description: The mode is the most common age: 18 or 19
The few older students pull the mean upward

sections.tip: When a few very high values are present (outliers), mean > median. When a few very low values are present, mean < median.

sections.title: Type 3: Finding a Missing Value Given a Condition
Example: Mean = Median Constraint
sections.problem:
A data set is: $6, 8, x, 12, 15$. The mean and median are equal. Which of the following could NOT be a value of $x$?

A) 6 \quad B) 11 \quad C) 16 \quad D) 21

steps.description: For the median: sort depends on x. If x is in the middle range, the median is x
Set mean = median = x (when x is in range 8-12)

sections.answer: Check each answer choice: the one that makes mean ≠ median is the answer.
sections.tip: When x's position changes the median, test the condition for each case separately.

sections.title: Type 4: Maximum, Range, and Frequency Tables
Example: Find Maximum from Frequency Table
sections.problem: A frequency table shows data values and how often each appears. The values range from 6 to 14. The value 13 has frequency 0. What is the maximum data value?

steps.description: The maximum is the largest value with nonzero frequency

sections.tip: For frequency tables: ignore values with frequency 0 when finding min/max. The minimum is the smallest nonzero-frequency value.

sections.title: Type 5: Box Plots and Comparing Data Sets
Reading a Box Plot
sections.content:
A **box plot** (box-and-whisker plot) shows five key values:

$$\text{Min} \quad | \quad Q_1 \quad | \quad \text{Median} \quad | \quad Q_3 \quad | \quad \text{Max}$$

- The **box** spans from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ (the interquartile range, IQR)
- The **line inside the box** is the **median**
- The **whiskers** extend to the min and max
- A **wider box** = more spread in the middle 50%

sections.title: Example: Compare Two Box Plots
sections.problem: Group 1 box plot: Min=21, Q1=22, Median=25, Q3=26, Max=28. Group 2 box plot: different values. Which group has the greater median?

steps.description: Read the median from each box plot (the line inside the box)
Compare: whichever median line is further right is larger

sections.answer: The group with the higher median line in the box plot has the greater median.
sections.tip: You can NEVER determine the mean from a box plot. Only median and spread (range, IQR) can be read directly.

sections.title: Type 6: Comparing Spread Between Two Sets
Example: Compare Spread from Summary Statistics
sections.problem: Group A heights: mean 70 in, median 69 in, range 8 in. Group B heights: mean 71 in, median 71 in, range 14 in. Which group has larger spread?

steps.description: Spread = how dispersed the data is. Range is one measure of spread

sections.answer: Group B has larger spread (range = 14 vs 8)

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: **Median:** sort the data; middle value for odd count; average of two middle values for even count
**Mean:** sum ÷ count. Mean is pulled toward outliers/skew
**Distribution shape:** right-skewed → mode < median < mean; symmetric → all three equal
**Box plots:** the line in the box = median; box width = IQR (middle 50%); mean is NOT shown
**Spread:** range = max − min; larger range or IQR = more spread

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Forgetting to sort before finding the median
- With even count: finding the middle one value instead of averaging the two middle values
- Confusing median with mean: they're different! Median is position-based, mean is sum-based
- Reading the mean from a box plot (impossible — box plots don't show the mean)
- In frequency tables: forgetting to repeat values according to their frequency when sorting

sat_tips: Always sort the data before finding the median
If a few extreme values are present, expect mean ≠ median — the mean gets pulled toward the outliers
Box plots show the median directly, but the mean requires calculation
For 'which value of x makes mean = median' problems, write out the mean formula and set it equal to the median formula, then solve
